messages:
devin: quick idea — I want to add a new rollout guard type: "slo-sentinel". It watches p95 latency, error-rate, and a token-cost burn rate per-tenant and can either throttle, divert to fallback model, or auto-pause the canary. sketch config below: ```json
{
  "type": "slo-sentinel",
  "checks": [{"metric": "p95_latency_ms", "threshold": 450}, {"metric": "error_rate", "threshold": 0.015}, {"metric": "token_burn_rate", "threshold": 1200}],
  "window_sec": 60,
  "action": "auto-pause",
  "cooldown_sec": 300
}
```

anya: love the name. couple points:
- token_burn_rate needs to be clarified: is it billed tokens or raw model tokens? cached prefixes will distort this if we don't normalize.
- autopause should surface reason codes for audit (so support/customers can see "p95_latency" vs "cost")

jamal: telemetry nit: make sure we emit both the raw metric event and a derived "slo_violation" event with {guard_id, tenant_id, value, action_taken}. that's what indexing and downstream dashboards will depend on. also: use snake_case metric names we already have (p95_latency_ms -> p95_latency_ms ok).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model rdx-v3 on service payments at 1969991120 — 5% traffic.

sam: UX thought — in the console timeline show a discrete "safety state" bubble for each rollout: OK / WATCH / PAUSED. WATCH should expand inline to show which check tripped and the metric sparkline. clicking the reason should open the telemetry trace.

ciara: defaults: 95th latency 450ms is reasonable for public tier, but we need per-tenant baselines. Suggest default policy = "relative to tenant baseline" where threshold = max(global_default, baseline * 1.5). avoids noisy autopause for high-latency legacy tenants.

kevin: instead of instant autopause, can we do a probabilistic backoff first? ex: on violation, reduce canary weight by 50% and re-evaluate in 30s; if still bad then pause. reduces false positives from transient spikes.

devin: good call. plan: make action enum = [notify, partial-divert, backoff, pause]. backoff has params {factor, reevaluate_sec, max_backoffs}.

anya: for cost checks we should use amortized token_cost_per_response to avoid punishing cached responses. Put an event annotation when cache hit so the guard can ignore cached hits if configured.

jamal: logging/metrics names: rollout.guard.violation, rollout.guard.action, rollout.state.transition. include guard_version so we can roll forward/back. This lets us query: "what rollouts did guard v2 auto-pause last 30d".

ciara: one more operational: add a tenant opt-out flag for autopause for enterprise customers that want manual control. must be audited.

sam: UI needs an override button with a mandatory text reason and TTL. no sticky overrides without separate approval flow.

devin: tests: unit for evaluator logic, e2e using traffic-sim that emits p95 spikes and synthetic token burn. also a smoke test for audit log entries. I'll draft a test matrix.

kevin: question re api: how does this config get to the runtime? we already have /rollouts/:id/guards. do we extend that schema or create /rollouts/:id/sentinels?

jamal: extend existing guards schema but keep a "kind" field so runtime can switch evaluator impls. backwards compatible if we default kind=basic-threshold.

deploy-bot: Canary update: 2% -> 1% after automated backoff triggered at 1969991153.

devin: action items: (1) I'll PR schema + evaluator impl (2) jamal will add telemetry events and docs for names (3) sam/ciara will mock console UX and override flow (4) anya/kevin work through cost normalization and backoff params. tagging owners on PRs.

anya: ping @devin once PR is up, I'll review the normalization piece. also add a short FAQ about noisy tenants.

devin: thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
